In most cases, a past therapist cannot share your information with a current therapist unless you give them explicit permission to do so. Mental health professionals are bound by strict privacy laws and ethical guidelines that protect your confidentiality. To share your records or discuss your treatment, they typically need you to sign a formal "Release of Information" document. 

You have the right to decide what information is shared and with whom. If you want your new therapist to have your past records to help with your current care, you can authorize that transfer. However, if you prefer to keep your past treatment completely private, you are entirely within your rights to withhold that consent. The only rare exceptions to this rule involve situations where there is an immediate risk of severe harm to yourself or others, or a court order, where therapists may be legally required to share information to ensure safety.
